_note: Source of truth for the Assumptions panel and ASSUMPTIONS.md. Run `npm run assumptions` to regenerate ASSUMPTIONS.md.

assumptions.text: Bluetooth hop selection is pseudo-random and uniform over the allowed set, not the exact specification kernel.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi contention is simplified, with no hidden nodes and no other networks.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Receiver desensitisation is a threshold model, not an RF model.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Packet durations come from tables, not from bit-level encoding.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Behaviour labelled "Implementations vary" (arbitration policy, priority table, isolation threshold, AFH delay) uses generic defaults and is configurable.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: No real RF power levels, path loss, or modulation errors are modelled in the prototype.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: EDR packet types (2-DH, 3-DH, 2-EV, 3-EV) use the same on-air occupancy as the basic-rate packet with the same slot count: 366, 1622 and 2870 us for 1, 3 and 5 slots.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The A2DP slave reply defaults to a 5-slot packet, taken literally from Example 1 ("5-slot slave replies in slot pairs"). Real devices usually reply with a short acknowledgement; a Reply packet parameter lets the user change it.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The base priority table has no entry for Classic ACL data, so one was added (BT_ACL_DATA, 35, just below A2DP). Channel Sounding and direction finding use this class.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The spec gives the critical priority for A2DP only (equal to isochronous audio, 90). For other buffered streams the critical priorities are 95 for LE Audio and 75 for Wi-Fi video streaming. All values are in priorityTable.json.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: "HFP" is treated as any SCO or eSCO voice link, tagged VOICE_LINK, because the profile has no air footprint of its own.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Platform fields were added beyond 7A.2 so that FR-8 to FR-14a and rules F-1, P-3 and T-6 can be evaluated: femArrangement, wifiChains, simultaneousWifiTxBtRx, wifiMultiRole, mloSimultaneousTxRx, btMaxVersion, timeShareBtPercent, timeShareSliceUs, afhDelayUs, guardMHz, interactionThresholdDb, and the device limits maxBleConnections, maxEscoLinks and maxIsoStreams. antennaMode and femArrangement are both stored so that rule F-1 can detect a contradiction.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Every Wi-Fi task has its own Channel and Bandwidth parameters. The value 0 means use the platform setting. This lets rule P-7 compare tasks, for example a station and a soft-AP.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: T-6 fires when access-point and station tasks are selected and the platform does not allow Wi-Fi multi-role. P-7 fires when two non-scanning Wi-Fi tasks use different channels or widths on a single core that is not in concurrent mode. Scans and roaming sweep many channels and are exempt.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: F-5 is read literally: it fires when the AFH minimum is greater than the number of Classic channels outside the Wi-Fi footprint plus guard, plus the protocol minimum of 20.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: W-1 fires when the window is shorter than twice a task's repeat interval (fewer than two events). One-shot and irregular-burst tasks are excluded.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: P-6 fires above 8 Bluetooth tasks, above 8 Wi-Fi tasks, or above 12 tasks in total. The thresholds are in limits.json.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The Classic slot budget counts, for each reserved or polling link, 2 times the packet slot count per pair, times the pairs, plus the retransmission window, divided by the interval. Only tasks that declare a slot reservation in the catalogue are counted.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi generations without aggregation (802.11a, b, g) carry one 1500 byte frame per burst. Control and management frames use the legacy preamble and a basic or control rate. Service and tail bits are not modelled. DIFS is SIFS plus two slot times.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The block estimate uses the expected number of events for irregular-burst tasks, rounded up, and always counts at least one event for each task.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Anchor flags: SCO, eSCO, sniff and HID are HIGH miss cost; LE Audio is MEDIUM; LE connection, periodic advertising, Classic ACL polling and Wi-Fi beacon or DTIM wake-ups are LOW. Beacon and DTIM protection and Classic ACL polling are labelled Implementations vary.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Target Wake Time and multi-link operation are gated by the Wi-Fi feature list (rule T-4). Rule T-1 compares a Wi-Fi task's minimum generation, which is empty for these two tasks, so one problem is never reported twice.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: BLE packet duration is fixed overhead plus (header, CRC and payload bytes) times microseconds per byte. Coded PHY fixed overhead covers preamble, access address, coding indicator and both terminators (400 us for S=8, 382 us for S=2).
assumptions.label: STANDARD

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi PHY rate is the highest modulation and coding scheme rate for one stream with a short guard interval, multiplied by the stream count. Rate step-down for retries multiplies this by factors in wifiTiming.json.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi scan channel lists are offered as two choices (1, 6, 11 and 1 to 13) and sweep 2.4 GHz channels. Scans on 5 and 6 GHz are not modelled.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The exclusive-pair table starts empty, as the spec says. Classic discovery tasks that overlap in time are scheduled one after the other by the engine.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The simulation window is a hard cutoff. A block that would start at or after the end of the window is not created. A block that starts inside the window keeps its full duration even if it ends after the window.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Random advertising delay (0 to 10 ms) is drawn once per event and accumulates: the next event is the previous one plus the interval plus that event's delay. Each task draws from its own random stream, derived from the seed and the task instance id, so adding a task never changes another task's random numbers.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: In Classic slot schedules the master packet starts in an even slot and the slave reply starts in the slot straight after the master packet ends; the next pair starts at the next even slot after the reply. Every Classic block is its own hop (each slot hops).
assumptions.label: STANDARD

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi medium access before each burst is DIFS plus a random backoff of 0 to 15 slots (the first packet of an event that transmits). Receive-only events such as beacon reception have no backoff. A burst that would overrun the next one pushes it back, so bursts of one task never overlap.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Reactive follow-ups of a scan window (SCAN_REQ and SCAN_RSP, CONNECT_IND) are placed straight after the window that triggered them, one set per window, or only after the first window for initiating.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Irregular bursts use exponentially distributed gaps (a Poisson process) with the requested average rate. A short window can therefore hold fewer bursts than the average suggests.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Wi-Fi multi-link operation sends bursts alternately on the selected links. The 2.4 GHz link uses the platform channel (width capped at 40 MHz); 5 GHz uses channel 36 and 6 GHz channel 5 unless changed in the data file.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The severity table in the spec has no row for Transmit against Transmit with no frequency overlap. It is filled in as HARD on a shared path and TOLERATED on separate paths. All cells are in conflictSeverity.json.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are forced to take turns (the "shared" column) when the antenna is shared, when the core mode is not CONCURRENT (a shared core), or, for Bluetooth receive against Wi-Fi transmit, when simultaneous Wi-Fi TX with Bluetooth RX is switched off. Otherwise isolation against the threshold picks the column.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A Bluetooth channel overlaps Wi-Fi when its footprint intersects the Wi-Fi footprint widened by the guard (open intervals). For Wi-Fi channel 6 at 20 MHz and a 1 MHz guard this is 2426 to 2448 MHz, which is 23 Classic channels. The spec text says "about 22".
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The AFH map avoids the operating channels of selected 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi tasks (including the 2.4 GHz link of multi-link operation). Scans and roaming sweeps are ignored. If fewer than the minimum channels remain, removed channels furthest from the Wi-Fi centre are put back first.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Each hop is a seeded uniform draw that is stored on the block. When AFH narrows the channel set, the same draw is mapped onto the reduced set, so a run is repeatable and only blocks after the AFH delay change. BLE advertising channels are not changed by AFH.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Retransmission blocks that were never triggered (eSCO window, spare ISO subevents) are not on the air and cannot conflict. A retry is a new block that does.
assumptions.label: STANDARD

assumptions.text: Only a Bluetooth block against a Wi-Fi block is arbitrated. Blocks of the same technology are not arbitrated against each other, but a block that arbitration moves or retries is never placed on top of another block of its own radio.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Blocks that belong together (a master packet and its reply, a Wi-Fi burst and its acknowledgement) move together when the first block is delayed. A later block cannot be delayed on its own: if it loses, it is denied and the whole group is retried. If the first block is denied, the rest of the group is not sent.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Once the first block of a pair has won, the rest of the pair keeps the priority it won with. Without this the buffer level, which drops as soon as the first packet is granted, would let Wi-Fi take the reply slot of a pair that had just won.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A DELAYED block moves to the earliest time after the winner's whole group has ended that is free of already granted blocks, of blocks on its own radio, and of waiting blocks that would beat it. Classic blocks are placed on an even slot, Wi-Fi blocks add DIFS. A block can be moved at most 16 times (limits.json), then it is denied.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A block moved past the end of the window keeps the status DELAYED and starts after the window. It still occupies its radio, so later moves queue behind it.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Packets waiting in a buffered stream are counted as packets planned so far minus packets delivered. Packets are interchangeable, so the oldest waiting packet is not forced to go first, and the delay shown for one block can be larger than the packet's real wait.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A retransmission of an anchor task is a fallback and is not protected: it competes as an ordinary block at priority 5 (priorityTable.json), below every class, so Wi-Fi wins it. Anchors with medium miss cost (LE Audio) are treated like high-cost anchors and are never given up.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Retry placement: Classic ACL at the next even slot after the pair; eSCO and LE Audio in an existing retransmission slot or spare subevent of the same event; other LE traffic after the next event of the same task; Wi-Fi after DIFS plus a new seeded backoff, with the data frame stretched by the next rate step. Retries stop at the retry limit (default 7) and the block is lost.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: TIME_SHARE gives each slice to one technology. Ownership follows a low-discrepancy sequence (golden-ratio steps from a seeded phase), so the long-run split equals the configured ratio and periodic traffic does not line up with one owner for ever. A plain alternating pattern would deny either none or all of a 30 ms BLE link in Example 5, because 30 ms is a multiple of 10 ms. The rule applies whenever the path is shared; a block outside its slice is denied (anchors) or delayed to its next slice, and an overlap inside a slice goes to the block that started first.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: In a DEGRADED conflict both blocks are marked DEGRADED and corrupted (interference is mutual in this simple model), and their airtime is still drawn. They are not delayed or denied.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A block with no overlap is GRANTED. A block whose only overlaps are TOLERATED is TOLERATED. A block in a WARNING conflict carries a warning flag. A block that was moved stays DELAYED even after it is granted.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The conflict list shows each overlap at its planned time, so a delayed block's original conflict stays listed, plus any overlap that appears only after a block moved. HARD conflicts are linked to the decision that settled them.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A packet is delivered when its whole group went out (a master packet and its reply, a Wi-Fi burst and its acknowledgement) with no block denied, lost or corrupted, and every block started inside the window. Retries count: a packet is delivered if any attempt in its chain was.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Throughput impact is the share of requested payload that was lost, corrupted, or still queued at the end of the window beyond what the task may hold. A buffered stream may hold up to its critical threshold (4 packets for A2DP) without penalty, because the rule is that no packet waits past the critical point. Packets queued at the end are always reported separately. Delay by itself is a latency effect, not a loss.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: For a buffered stream, latency matches the i-th delivery with the i-th packet to arrive (a queue), so the figure is the real wait in the buffer and not the distance a single block was moved.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Overlap airtime is measured at the planned positions of first-attempt blocks and counts every time overlap of a Bluetooth and a Wi-Fi block, even when the pair cannot interact. The frequency part uses the Wi-Fi footprint plus guard.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Anchors hit and missed are counted per planned event: an event is a hit only if all its blocks went out on time and uncorrupted. The time left before the supervision timeout is the timeout minus the longest gap between events that went out, including the start and end of the window.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The spec does not give the Wi-Fi video bitrate. The Example 1 preset uses 150 Mbps on a 20 MHz, 2x2 Wi-Fi 7 link, which keeps the stream close to continuous. The catalogue default for the Video streaming task stays at 100 Mbps. At 150 Mbps A2DP is delayed while it has fewer than four packets waiting, becomes critical at four and delays Wi-Fi bursts, no A2DP block is lost, A2DP impact is 0 and Wi-Fi impact is about 7 percent.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: "Every Bluetooth block that overlaps in time with a Wi-Fi block is a HARD conflict" is read together with the severity table in 7A.7: with a shared antenna, a receive against a receive is TOLERATED, and every overlap that involves a transmit is HARD, whatever the frequency.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The DEGRADED share is measured over all Bluetooth blocks that overlap a Wi-Fi block in time over the 1 second window, with Wi-Fi video as the traffic. With the 23 channels inside the footprint plus guard the result is 26.6 percent, inside the 28 percent plus or minus 5 point band. Over blocks whose conflict involves a transmit it is about 29 percent.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Example 5 uses the TIME_SHARE slice pattern described in A-42. With a 30 ms interval and 2M PHY, 16 of 34 first-attempt events are denied, each retry follows the next event by one interval, and the added latency for the retried packets is about 30.6 ms. Wi-Fi web browsing is sparse, so the denials come from the slice schedule, not from a Wi-Fi block being on the air.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Dense areas use level of detail: when blocks are too small or too many, the time view draws density bars (one bar per 4 pixels per lane), and individual blocks only when zoomed in. This bounds the number of drawn elements, so SVG is used throughout and no canvas layer was needed. With more than 20,000 blocks, panning measured at the display refresh rate (60 frames per second) in headless Chromium at every zoom level tried. Revisit canvas if a slower machine shows otherwise.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: Both light-theme lane backgrounds are white, because the spec orange (#E8710A) only just reaches 3 to 1 on white. The spec grey for removed channels (#9AA0A6) is 2.6 to 1 on white, so removed channels also carry a darker dotted mark (#5F6368). Amber against red and against orange is close for red-green colour blindness; those pairs are told apart by pattern (hatch against strike, hatch over a solid block), as the spec asks for a pattern with every colour.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: At 1x speed the whole simulation window plays in 10 seconds. The speeds 0.1x, 0.5x, 1x and 5x scale that. Step to next event stops at every block start and every conflict start.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The suggestions in the explanation panel are chosen from the conflict: separate antennas for a shared-antenna conflict, adaptive hopping for a frequency overlap on 2.4 GHz, more isolation for a low-isolation conflict, and Bluetooth-favoured arbitration for a hard conflict under the priority policy. At most three are shown. Applying one re-runs the scenario and reports the before and after counts.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The sentence "What it means for the user" is built from the task tags and the final status of each block: audio, voice, anchor links and Wi-Fi throughput each have their own wording, with a generic fallback.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The waterfall draws hops of blocks that went out (granted, delayed, tolerated or degraded). Blocks that were denied are not drawn there, and the planned position of a delayed block is shown in the time view only.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: A delayed block that was moved past the end of the window is shown by its dashed ghost at the planned time with an arrow running to the edge of the view.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: At most 300 blocks in view are reachable with the Tab key, to keep keyboard navigation usable; every block still has an accessible description, and the conflict markers and the conflict list reach every conflict.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

assumptions.text: The browser checks in e2e/ open the page with ?e2e, which exposes a small hook to load a generated scenario. The hook is not used by the application itself.
assumptions.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES
